label: Он
description: Third-person masculine singular sentences for understanding verb agreement and predicate behavior.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Third-person singular motion. 1. 'Он' makes the subject masculine singular. 2. 'Идет' is the correct third-person form of motion on foot. 3. 'Домой' keeps the destination natural and clear.

Strategic focus: Third-person present tense. 1. 'Читает' marks the subject as third person singular. 2. 'Книгу' is the direct object and stays concrete. 3. This sentence helps learners hear how the verb changes when the subject shifts from I/you/we to he.

Strategic focus: Simple transitive action. 1. 'Пишет' is the correct masculine singular present form. 2. 'Письмо' stays easy to picture. 3. The sentence is practical and keeps attention on the verb ending.

Strategic focus: Perception in third person. 1. 'Видит' is the masculine singular form. 2. 'Стол' is a stable direct object. 3. This sentence helps establish that third-person verbs still carry clear agreement markers.

Strategic focus: Emotion plus demonstrative. 1. 'Любит' is the third-person singular present form. 2. 'Этот дом' matches the masculine noun. 3. This sentence is natural and useful for seeing demonstrative agreement.

Strategic focus: Irregular verb in third person. 1. 'Ест' is the correct third-person form of 'есть'. 2. 'Хлеб' keeps the object practical. 3. This sentence is important because it trains one of the most common irregular forms in Russian.

Strategic focus: Survival vocabulary and aspect of action. 1. 'Пьет' is third-person singular. 2. 'Воду' remains a clear accusative object. 3. This sentence is highly useful in everyday conversation and easy to remember.
Strategic focus: Negation in third person. 1. 'Не' negates the verb. 2. 'Понимает' is the correct third-person form. 3. This sentence is extremely useful for communication and problem-solving.

Strategic focus: Desire and direct address. 1. 'Хочет' is the proper third-person singular form. 2. 'Кофе' keeps the sentence practical. 3. This is a common, natural line that models ordinary Russian conversation.

Strategic focus: Activity and place. 1. 'Работает' is third-person singular. 2. 'Дома' makes the location adverbial and natural. 3. This sentence helps learners see how the verb changes while the place word remains unchanged.

Strategic focus: Language use. 1. 'Говорит' is the correct masculine singular form. 2. 'По-русски' is the natural adverbial language phrase. 3. This sentence is a core identity statement for learners.
Strategic focus: Knowledge statement. 1. 'Знает' is third-person singular. 2. 'Это' points at the known item. 3. The sentence is compact and very useful for practicing subject-verb-object flow.

Strategic focus: Taking an object. 1. 'Берет' marks third-person singular. 2. 'Книгу' is the object being taken. 3. This sentence reinforces how a single noun can be acted on by a verb that changes with the subject.

Strategic focus: Physical action. 1. 'Открывает' is the masculine singular present form. 2. 'Дверь' is a simple object. 3. This sentence is ideal for repeated typing practice because it is vivid and easy to understand.
Strategic focus: Perception verb. 1. 'Слышит' is third-person singular. 2. 'Музыку' is the object heard. 3. This sentence shows how perception verbs also follow the same person-number system.

Strategic focus: Object pronoun form. 1. 'Видит' is the masculine singular present form. 2. 'Меня' is the object form of 'я'. 3. This sentence teaches pronoun alternation when the pronoun stops being the subject.

Strategic focus: Routine action. 1. 'Делает' is a highly flexible third-person verb. 2. 'Чай' gives the sentence a practical everyday object. 3. This is a good sentence for showing how ordinary Russian can be very compact.
Strategic focus: Carrying. 1. 'Несет' is the correct third-person singular form. 2. 'Сумку' is the carried object. 3. This sentence is useful for action verbs that naturally require an object.

Strategic focus: Finding something. 1. 'Находит' is the masculine singular present form. 2. 'Ключ' is a common everyday noun. 3. The sentence is practical and reinforces the person-number contrast with other pronouns.

Strategic focus: Verb governance and prepositional case. 1. 'Думает' is third-person singular. 2. 'О работе' demonstrates the prepositional form after 'о'. 3. This sentence is especially good for teaching that verbs shape the form of the words they govern.
